name: Buenos Aires
tagline: Bife de chorizo with a Michelin star, a café haunted by Borges, and a neighborhood joint's milanesa that's already in the guide.

Don Julio.description: The world's most acclaimed steakhouse: a Michelin star, a green star for sustainability, and #1 on Latin America's 50 Best.

Café Tortoni.description: Buenos Aires' oldest café, since 1858. Borges, Gardel, and Cortázar all sat at its marble tables.

El Preferido de Palermo.description: A corner joint since 1952, now recognized by the Michelin Guide. The thin-cut steak milanesa is on another level.

Aramburu.description: A tasting menu of high technical precision from chef Gonzalo Aramburu, in Recoleta. Two Michelin stars.

Crizia.description: An oyster and seasonal fish specialist in Palermo. One Michelin star.
